newsitem.title: USA: CSCE world Oct sugar ends down, back months higher.
newsitem.headline: CSCE world Oct sugar ends down, back months higher.

text.p: CSCE world July sugar futures settled tightly mixed as a three-day speculative buying spree came to a close, market sources said.

The spot July contract ended down 0.04 cent at 11.11 cents per lb, traded 11.19 to 11.10 cents. October settled 0.01 cent lower at 11.25 cents, while the rest of the board finished 0.01 and 0.02 cent higher.
The back four contracts climbed to new lifetime highs before ending the day only barely firmer, while the front months stood over unchanged for most of the day.
Steady producer selling, particularly in the most-active October contract, emerged in the afternoon to chip away at gains and pressure the market to the day's lows.
The trade was a persistent seller of the July/October and the October/March spreads, dealers said.
The nearby switch closed at a 0.14 cent premium basis October, compared with 0.11 cent on Wednesday's close.
Traders said the market is likely to follow-through to the downside on Friday but said the benchmark October contract is not expected to break out of its recent trading range.
Nearby resistance was pegged at 11.34 cents followed by 11.42 cents in October, and support at 11.00 and then at 10.96 cents.
The July contract expires on June 30. Open interest July fell by 4,678 lots to 24,097 lots, as of Wednesday.
An estimated 19,485 lots changed hands on the day, compared with Wednesday's official 37,079 lots.
